models.title: Marginal consumption response to additional disposable income
models.summary: Citation correction to prior r1: MPC is the share of an additional disposable-income unit that is spent; the remainder is MPS.

relationship.original_equation: MPC=delta consumption / delta disposable income; MPS=1-MPC
relationship.locator: Section D: d-the-expenditure-output-model; exact subsection stated in evidence
relationship.translation_notes: Both changes have currency dimensions, giving a fraction. MPS=1-MPC is the complementary allocation from the same partition and is retained here as a special solve/composition note. Nonzero income change is enforced as dY squared positive because the engine has no != operator. Revisionr2 replaces an insufficient or inaccessible corroboration locator with a directly inspected page containing the actual formula definition; equation and numeric cases unchanged. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

assumptions: Source assumption: other consumption determinants are held fixed.
Source model: a conventional positive marginal allocation has0<=MPC<=1; this is an economic scope condition, not required by division alone.
limitations: A finite difference is a local marginal response only if the response is linear over that interval or interpreted in the infinitesimal limit.
Average propensity C/Y is distinct and is not a reliable general estimator of MPC.
